Which firm appears most prepared: The comparison can be made only partially on this evidence. The firms disclose very different evidence for preparedness, and no common metric for wealth-transfer capture is published across all five, so no single firm can be ranked as most prepared on a like-for-like basis. On the specific grounds that are disclosed, Schwab is the only firm that publishes a direct retention metric for wealth transfers (approximately 75% of assets retained in a wealth transfer event), and it states its retail business is built to win across generations with an extremely high retention rate; Morgan Stanley discloses a 99% client retention rate and 20-year relationship durations but does not quantify wealth-transfer retention specifically; Merrill discloses leadership in next-generation advisor talent (446 advisors on the 2025 Forbes list) but not a wealth-transfer retention figure; Raymond James discloses intergenerational wealth strategies and advisor succession retention but no wealth-transfer retention percentage; and Edward Jones discloses that generational wealth transfers outside the firm are a drag on net new assets, the opposite evidence of the other firms. Because these measures are not defined on a common basis (different units, scopes, and periods), they cannot be validly compared or ranked across firms.

adjacent.text: Morgan Stanley: For the Wealth and Investment Management basis, total client assets grew to $9.3 trillion at year-end 2025, supported by over $350 billion in net new assets; and stood at $10 trillion in the second quarter of 2026.
adjacent.differs_because: Total client assets is a stock measure, not a direct measure of wealth-transfer capture; the basis (Wealth and Investment Management) differs from the Wealth Management figures.

adjacent.text: Morgan Stanley: For the Wealth Management basis, total client assets stood at $8 trillion in the second quarter of 2026, and $8.4 trillion in the third quarter of 2026.
adjacent.differs_because: Total client assets is a stock measure and covers a different basis (Wealth Management) from the Wealth and Investment Management figures.

adjacent.text: Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley reported full-year 2024 net new assets of $251.7 billion and full-year 2025 net new assets of $356.3 billion.
adjacent.differs_because: Net new assets is a proxy figure, not a direct measure of wealth-transfer capture.

adjacent.text: Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley reported fourth quarter 2025 net new assets of $122.3 billion, first quarter 2026 net new assets of $118 billion, record second quarter 2026 net new assets of $148 billion, and third quarter 2026 net new assets of $232 billion.
adjacent.differs_because: Net new assets is a proxy figure, not a direct measure of wealth-transfer capture.

adjacent.text: Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley stated it retains 99% of its clients, and that 60% of advisor-led assets are associated with clients having an average relationship duration of 20 years, as of the fourth quarter of 2024.
adjacent.differs_because: Client retention rate and relationship duration are indicative proxies, not a direct measure of wealth-transfer capture.

adjacent.text: Morgan Stanley: In the first quarter of 2026, Morgan Stanley noted greater asset retention from its Workplace channel, as vested assets were retained and migrated into the advisor-led channel.
adjacent.differs_because: Workplace asset retention is a channel-specific proxy, not a direct measure of wealth-transfer capture.

adjacent.text: The Charles Schwab Corporation: Schwab states it retains approximately 75% of assets in a wealth transfer event, presented as its 'RETAIN' metric.
adjacent.differs_because: This is a direct wealth-transfer retention rate, but it is Schwab's own metric and not comparable to other firms' disclosures.

adjacent.text: The Charles Schwab Corporation: In the third quarter of 2026, Schwab's CEO stated the firm's retention rate around wealth transfers is extremely high and that Schwab is winning assets with all generations.
adjacent.differs_because: This is a qualitative statement, not a quantified figure.

adjacent.text: The Charles Schwab Corporation: Schwab's total client assets reached $11.90 trillion at December 31, 2025 (up 18%), increased to $13.08 trillion at June 30, 2026 (up 10% from year-end), and rose to $10.10 trillion as of year-end 2024 (up 19% from year-end 2023).
adjacent.differs_because: Total client assets is a stock measure, not a direct measure of wealth-transfer capture.

adjacent.text: The Charles Schwab Corporation: Core net new assets totaled $366.9 billion in 2024 (up 20%), $519.4 billion in 2025 (up 42%), $119.8 billion in the second quarter of 2026 (up 49%), and $190.4 billion in the third quarter of 2026.
adjacent.differs_because: Core net new assets is a flow proxy, not a direct measure of wealth-transfer capture.

adjacent.text: Edward Jones: Edward Jones reported net new assets of $74 billion for 2025, relatively flat compared to 2024, and ended 2025 with 20,425 financial advisors.

adjacent.text: Edward Jones: Edward Jones ended the first quarter of 2026 with $2,417 billion of total client assets under care (AUC) and $1,064 billion of advisory programs AUC, and reported net new assets of $18 billion and 6.8 million client households.
